newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Pernas sees better profits in 97/98 year.
newsitem.headline: Pernas sees better profits in 97/98 year.

text.p: Malaysian property, hotels and plantations group Pernas International Holdings Bhd said on Wednesday it expects to improve its profit growth for the year ending January 31, 1998.

"From the performance so far, we are quite confident we would do better this year over last year, in terms of percentage of growth and profits also," Pernas chairman and chief executive officer Tunku Shahriman Tunku Sulaiman told reporters after the company's annual meeting. He did not elaborate.
The company reported net profit growth of 86.7 percent to 79.18 million ringgit for the year ended January 31, 1997, with an earnings per share rise of 55.2 percent to 17.7 cents.
The current financial year is the company's first full year under a privatised management following a management buyout of government assets by a team led by Tunku Shahriman.
He said Pernas was looking to separately list its other subsidiaries, after the planned separate listing of plantations assets held under 51-percent owned Tradewinds (M) Bhd.

"We are looking into it (separate listings). We have appointed advisors," Tunku Shahriman said. "We may group assets which we think would get good consideration from the SC (Securities Commission)", he said without elaborating.
